key_insight: ClinStigma provides a clinician-guided way to build synthetic benchmarks that test whether models can recognize stigmatizing language in clinical notes, including hard gray-zone cases.
clinical_relevance: This could help developers and hospitals evaluate clinical NLP systems more safely and consistently before use in real documentation workflows.
method: Generated candidate clinical sentences with a frontier LLM.
Clinicians iteratively reviewed and refined an annotation rubric for stigmatizing, neutral, and ambiguous language.
Evaluated three open-weight LLMs with zero-shot prompts and tested external generalization on annotated MIMIC-IV documentation.
evidence_signal: The benchmark included 500 clinician-adjudicated sentences with very high agreement (kappa 0.976 overall), and external testing on 3,716 MIMIC-IV examples achieved 84.4% accuracy and 0.824 macro F1.
watch_item: Because the benchmark is synthetic and the ambiguous class remained difficult for models, performance may not fully reflect real-world clinical documentation complexity.
paper_title: ClinStigma: A Clinician-Guided Framework for Developing Synthetic Benchmarks of Contextual Stigmatizing Language in Clinical Documentation
